import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# --- Data Preprocessing ---
# Combine date and time into a single datetime object
df['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'] + ' ' + df['time'])

# Extract the hour of the day
df['hour'] = df['datetime'].dt.hour

# --- Data Aggregation ---
# Create a pivot table to aggregate total sales by product and hour
sales_pivot = df.pivot_table(
    index='product',
    columns='hour',
    values='total',
    aggfunc='sum'
).fillna(0)

# Ensure all hours from 0 to 23 are present for a complete heatmap,
# in case some hours had no sales at all.
all_hours = pd.DataFrame(index=sales_pivot.index, columns=range(24)).fillna(0)
sales_pivot = sales_pivot.reindex(columns=all_hours.columns, fill_value=0)


# --- Visualization ---
# Set the style and create the figure
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", font_scale=0.9)
plt.figure(figsize=(18, 9))

# Create the heatmap
heatmap = sns.heatmap(
    sales_pivot,
    cmap="YlGnBu",  # A sequential color map is good for this kind of data
    linewidths=.5,
    annot=False,   # Annotations would be too cluttered
    cbar_kws={'label': 'Total Sales ($)'} # Label for the color bar
)

# Customize titles and labels for clarity
heatmap.set_title(
    'Peak Sales Hours by Product',
    fontsize=20,
    fontweight='bold',
    pad=25
)
heatmap.set_xlabel('Hour of Day (24-hour format)', fontsize=12, labelpad=15)
heatmap.set_ylabel('Product', fontsize=12, labelpad=15)

# Improve tick label readability
plt.xticks(rotation=0, ha='center')
plt.yticks(rotation=0)

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
